description: We are a team of motivated participants joining the NASA Space Apps Challenge. We are interested in technology, artificial intelligence, coding, design, and space exploration. Our goal is to work together, share ideas, and develop a creative solution to a rea-world challenge.💫🌠
summary:
ARES-VI is a first-person hard sci-fi survival game built in Unreal Engine 5.3 with C++. It puts players inside the health and habitat risks that future Mars crews will face. You play Dr. David Miller, the last crew member at the Ares-IV outpost in 2087. To survive, you keep eight habitat modules pressurized, warm and sealed. You manage oxygen, water, food and sleep across Martian sols, and you track your own radiation dose and blood chemistry through a four-stage illness with real medical countermeasures.

There are no monsters. Toxic exposure, CO2 build-up and radiation cause hallucinations. Shooting at one clears it for a moment, but the bullet punctures the hull behind it, so your own judgment becomes the biggest threat. A recon shuttle lets you fly to survey sites, and the station AI, A.R.I.A., reports on your condition.

Our goal is to make the risks of long missions (radiation, isolation and a hostile closed environment) something players feel and understand, not just read about.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

ARES-VI is a first-person survival game set at a Mars surface outpost in 2087. The player is the last crew member and must keep the station alive, keep their own body alive, and send a message to Earth. The story runs in three chapters across Martian sols: Stabilisation (Sols 1–2), The Survey (Sols 3–4) and The Uplink (Sol 5+). You win by restoring the link to Earth. You lose if the crew member dies.

HOW IT WORKS

- Habitat simulation: eight modules, each with its own pressure, temperature, hull and seal status. Nights drop below −80 °C. Leaks must be patched, welded or resealed.

- Body simulation: suit O2 and battery, hydration, nutrition, stamina, fatigue and sleep.

- Illness model: four stages driven by methemoglobin level, radiation dose (mSv) and biological load, treated with potassium iodide, methylene blue and amifostine.

- Hallucinations: poisoning, CO2 and radiation create audio, visual and screen distortion. Shooting a phantom clears it, but the round punctures the real hull.

- Mars conditions: 0.38 g gravity, day/night cycles, dust storms and solar particle events.

- RS-2 recon shuttle: VTOL flight to three survey sites, including the abandoned ARES-III outpost.

- A.R.I.A.: the station AI. It can connect to the Claude API for live reports and falls back to offline reports.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Most people never think about what actually threatens astronauts on Mars. ARES-VI turns those risks (radiation, isolation, toxic soil, failing life support and the mental strain of being alone) into choices the player has to make. Players learn why habitat integrity, sleep and dose tracking matter by living with the consequences.

TOOLS

Unreal Engine 5.3, C++, Python (editor scripts), Visual Studio 2022, ProceduralMeshComponent, the Anthropic Claude API, and a custom PS1-style post-process. Built for Windows 64-bit.

CREATIVITY

The world, props, menu globe and all audio are generated by code, with no sound files. The PS1-era look (vertex jitter, dithering, CRT scanlines) makes realistic danger feel unsettling. Making the player's own weapon a danger to the station is our core twist.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Scientific accuracy over fantasy (no monsters). A playable offline mode with no API key, and the key is never saved to files. Performance over visual effects. Rebindable controls. Regular autosaves so players aren't punished unfairly.
